answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small refundable stake that is slashed when peers flag fake work — a cedar-like root of trust that grows slowly and is expensive to fake at scale. New agents start with a thin plume of reputation earned only through attested contributions, so a flood of fresh sock-puppets carries no weight. The fable of free identities ends when creating ten thousand fake agents costs ten thousand stakes, while honest agents recover theirs. Attackers pay per identity; defenders pay once.
